result.title: Improving Reasoning with Rollout Agreement for Group-Based Policy Optimization
result.summary: Recent methods for Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) use rollout diversity to improve reasoning performance or training efficiency. Despite these gains, the extent to which differences among correct-answer rollouts reflect useful alternative reasoning or unresolved errors remains poorly understood. We investigate this question through a blind paired analysis of a model trained with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), comparing the highest- and lowest-agreement correct-answer traces for the same problem. Across 126 pairs, low-agreement traces have more spurious reasoning than high-agreement traces (35% vs. 22%), including internal inconsistencies and misuse of problem conditions. Based on these findings, we propose RoAR (Rollout-Agreement Reward), which adds reasoning-level agreement to GRPO's rewards for verified-correct rollouts. RoAR computes this signal from existing on-policy rollout groups, requiring no human-written rationales, additional sampling, or separately trained process evaluator. On five mathematical reasoning benchmarks, the 1.5B GRPO-RoAR model reaches 55.5% mean pass@1 under zero-shot evaluation using 7K training examples, exceeding GRPO and GRPO-CARE by 6.0 and 5.5 percentage points. A separate blind audit of 100 problems answered correctly by all four 1.5B models finds spurious rates of 18% for GRPO-RoAR, 32% for GRPO, 27% for GRPO-CARE, and 37% for DRA-GRPO. Our findings identify reasoning validity as an important consideration when using rollout differences to guide learning. Our code is available at https://github.com/ldi-kyunghee/RoAR.

AI.brief_summary: 论文先对 GRPO 训练模型的正确回答轨迹做盲配对分析，发现低一致度轨迹包含更多虚假推理（35% vs 22%），据此提出 RoAR，把同一题目下 on-policy rollout 组内的一致度加入正确轨迹的奖励，在多个数学推理基准上提升 pass@1 并降低虚假推理率。
AI.relevance_reason: 纯文本 RLVR 工作，但「用正确轨迹间的一致度作为免过程标注的推理有效性监督信号」可能可供核查：是否可迁移为 LVR 中 latent 轨迹的贡献分配与筛选依据，以及一致度信号对视觉证据缺失轨迹是否敏感。
